# Spec: Extension build artifacts must not dirty the release tree

## 1. Intent

### Goal
Stop the reference-extension signing step from leaving untracked files in the
repository root, which makes goreleaser refuse to release.

### Business value
v0.20.0 signed the extension successfully — the first time that step ever ran —
and then died at goreleaser with `git is in a dirty state`, naming the two
artifacts the signing step had just written. The release never published.

The `.gitignore` already carried this exact fix for `compatibility-report.md`,
with a comment recording the same failure from the pipeline's first full run.
The lesson was written down and then not applied to the next generated artifact,
which is the part worth fixing beyond the two filenames.

### Constraints
- The artifacts must stay in the repository root: goreleaser publishes them via
  `extra_files`, whose globs resolve from there.

### Non-goals
- Changing how the extension is signed or published.

---

## 2. Requirements

### Functional
- R1: Artifacts generated by the release pipeline before goreleaser runs shall
  be ignored by Git, so the working tree stays clean at release time.
- R2: The ignore entry shall say why it exists, so the next generated artifact
  inherits the reasoning rather than repeating the failure.

### Non-functional
- No change to what is published: the same two files still ship as release
  assets.

### Security
- Ignoring build output must not hide a source file: both entries name exact
  generated filenames, not a pattern.

### Compatibility
- No product change.

---

## 3. Technical Plan

### Affected areas
- `.gitignore` — the two generated extension artifacts.

### Artifacts
- created: .pose/specs/pose-extension-signing-clean-tree/spec.md
- modified: .gitignore

### Delivery targets
- governance:extension-signing-clean-tree module:pose-mcp profile:release-governance entrypoint:pose-mcp/cmd/pose/main.go

### API/contract changes
- None.

### Technical risks
- An ignored filename that later becomes a real source file would be invisible
  to Git. Both names are unambiguous build output.

## 6. Validation

### Strategy
The failure is only reproducible in a release run, so the local proof is that
Git ignores both artifacts and that the release gates stay green. The real
confirmation is the next cut reaching goreleaser.

### Deterministic checks

#### Security / Contract
- Command: `git check-ignore -v pose-rule-kubernetes.tar.gz pose-rule-kubernetes.sigstore.json`
- Scope: both generated artifacts
- Expected: both resolve to the new .gitignore entries

### Execution log
- Date: 2026-08-07
- Environment: linux/amd64, Go 1.26.5, pose 0.20.1-dev.
- Notes: run 31209615394 shows `Sign the reference extension` passing and
  goreleaser failing immediately after, listing exactly the two files.

### Results summary
- Successes: both artifacts ignored; compatibility gate and strict gates green
- Failures: none
- Warnings: goreleaser reaching completion is only provable on the next cut

### Requirement trace
- R1 [satisfied] governance:extension-signing-clean-tree evidence:integration check:delivery-integration check:git-check-ignore — both artifacts resolve to .gitignore entries, so the tree is clean when goreleaser runs
- R2 [satisfied] report:.gitignore — the entry names the v0.20.0 failure and the spec, beside the identical `compatibility-report.md` entry it should have been modelled on

### Known gaps
- Proving goreleaser completes requires a release run; this cut is that proof.

---

## 7. Final Report

### Delivered scope
Both generated extension artifacts are ignored by Git, with a comment recording
the failure that made it necessary.

### Files and modules changed
- .gitignore

### Validation executed
- Command: `git check-ignore -v pose-rule-kubernetes.tar.gz pose-rule-kubernetes.sigstore.json`
- Result: both ignored

### Residual risks
- The pattern will recur: any future step that writes to the root before
  goreleaser has the same failure mode, and nothing enforces the rule.

### Follow-ups

- [open] Make the release workflow fail loudly and early on an unexpectedly dirty tree, naming the step that dirtied it, instead of letting goreleaser report it after the expensive gates have already run. (owner:@pose-maintainers crit:medium review:2026-10-02)
